extracted.intended_audience: Joint force commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), Joint Staff, combatant commands, and PA planners
extracted.subtask_description: Doctrine and authoritative guidance for planning, coordinating, executing, and assessing public affairs (PA) support to joint military operations, including strategic communication, media relations, domestic operations, and PA organization and resources. Intended to govern PA activity across the range of military operations and interagency/multinational contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information shall be made fully and readily available, consistent with statutory requirements, unless its release is precluded by national security constraints or valid statutory mandates or exceptions. A free flow of general and military information shall be made available without censorship or propaganda. Information will not be classified or otherwise withheld from criticism or to protect the government from embarrassment. Information shall be withheld only when disclosure would adversely affect national security or threaten the safety or privacy of the men and women of the Armed Forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support FOIA in both letter and spirit; coordinate with other government agencies (OGAs) as necessary to expedite flow; withhold only for valid security/privacy reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenet — Tell the Truth
rubrics_metrics.description: PA personnel will release only accurate information or officially released information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credibility is paramount; avoid releasing unverified information. Propaganda is prohibited; truthful releases build and preserve public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenet — Provide Timely and Accurate Information and Imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders should be prepared to release timely, factual, coordinated, and approved information and imagery about military operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness reduces adversary exploitation and counters misinformation; PA planning should reduce lag between events and public communication; imagery should be accurate and approved through security review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenet — Practice Security at the Source
rubrics_metrics.description: All DOD personnel and DOD contractors are responsible for safeguarding sensitive information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate OPSEC into PA planning; perform security reviews prior to release to prevent jeopardizing ongoing/future operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenet — Provide Consistent Information at All Levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The public often receives simultaneous information from a variety of official DOD sources at various levels; PA should ensure consistency across those levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate messages across staff, subordinate and supporting commanders, and interagency partners to avoid contradictory statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenet — Tell the DOD Story
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders designate official spokespeople, but they should educate and encourage military personnel, civilian employees, and contractors to tell the DOD story by providing them with timely information appropriate for public release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance broad information sharing with controls on official spokesperson designation; train internal audiences to convey approved themes without diverging from PAG.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA Mission
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of joint PA is to plan, coordinate, and synchronize US military public information activities and resources in order to support the commander's intent and concept of operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs advise the JFC on implications of decisions, plan/execute/evaluate PA activities, integrate PA with information operations, and assess foreign audience perceptions for planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA Role — Providing Trusted Counsel to Leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: PA core competency includes anticipating and advising JFCs on the possible impact of military operations and activities within the public information realm, preparing commanders to communicate, and analyzing the information environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs should be part of planning/decisionmaking, provide lessons learned, and have appropriate clearances to participate in command processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA Role — Enhancing Morale and Readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: PA activities enable military personnel and their families to understand roles, policies, and operations that affect them, thereby enhancing morale and readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Command information should create awareness of organizational goals and developments and equip internal audiences to act as ambassadors.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA Role — Fostering Public Trust and Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective PA builds public trust and understanding for the military's contribution to national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained, credible information releases and engagement underpin public support; PA should aim to strengthen these relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA Role — Creating Global Understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ PA with other information capabilities to develop and implement communication strategies that inform audiences about the impact of U.S. military operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synchronize PA with diplomatic, interagency, and multinational partners; tailor messaging to international audiences and cultural contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preeminence of Information (Timeliness and First Impressions)
rubrics_metrics.description: First impressions and timeliness strongly affect perceptions; adversaries can exploit speed to spread misleading information faster than corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders should be prepared to assume some risk to ensure timeliness; anticipate and plan for rapid information dissemination to shape first impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recency and Repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Recency and repetition increase newsworthiness and information retention; information must be timely, repeated, and delivered via multiple sources to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain continuous public engagement and repeated messaging across the operation to reinforce strategic communication themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of Culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Culture, ideology, and ethnocentric perspectives influence how news is produced and consumed; PA must account for cultural framing when crafting messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop culturally attuned messages; anticipate how audiences' cultural lenses will shape interpretation of events and visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of Propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Adversary propaganda uses the same newsworthy factors (conflict, imagery) to influence audiences; anticipate exploitation and preempt or respond rapidly to counter it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preemptively release appropriate information when feasible; prepare rapid response plans to counter misinformation and adversary narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA Planning Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: PA planning must identify requirements early (facilities, personnel, equipment, transport, comms), synchronize across staff and with partners, and consider augmentation and procurement because PA requirements often exceed available resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with supporting commands, Services, host nation, country team, OGAs, IGOs, and NGOs; include legal and security review processes in planning; identify resource shortfalls early.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs must assess public support and media environments using media analysis, polling data, and professional assessments to evaluate understanding of objectives and levels of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate assessments into planning and decisionmaking; use assessment to recommend PA structure and messaging adjustments and to evaluate impact of actions on perceptions, attitudes, and beliefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credentialing Journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for credentialing journalists are established by the Joint Force PAO or the MOC director; credentialing validates individuals as journalists and provides information to enhance reporting ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credentialing is not a control or means to restrict outlets; it helps ensure journalists receive support, are recognized under law of war if captured, and facilitates access without limiting free reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Ground Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground rules protect DOD personnel by preventing release of information that could threaten security or safety while facilitating media access to timely, relevant information. Ground rules also include requirements to protect media safety and welfare and are not intended to prevent release of derogatory or embarrassing information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground rules reconcile media access needs with security; explicitly state constraints (locations, timing, photography limits, safety requirements) and are to be applied to balance transparency and OPSEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Operations Center (MOC) — Establishment and Role
rubrics_metrics.description: A MOC is a central point of contact between the military and media during joint operations; it coordinates media operations, supports the JFC through the PAO, and should be established early to facilitate responsive media support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOCs should be staffed to support local/regional non-English media, coordinate media credentialing and access, and may also support command information activities; MOCs may be a center or section depending on scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Information Center (JIC) — Location and Use
rubrics_metrics.description: A JIC may be established in domestic/incident responses to coordinate release of emergency/incident-related information; it is normally located close to the best sources of information (incident command post or emergency operations center).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use JICs to coordinate across agencies; if no JIC exists, ensure robust coordination between DOD, primary agency, and other responders to provide timely public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic Operations — PA Phases (Shaping, Engagement, Transition)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD PA support in domestic operations evolves through Shaping (manage expectations, develop themes/messages), Engagement (on-scene informing via releases, press conferences, site visits), and Transition (articulate why DOD support is no longer required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor PA activities by phase; in Shaping focus on scope/timing messages, in Engagement support media and public with timely details, in Transition emphasize rationale for disengagement and handoff to other agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of Propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Propaganda has no place in DOD PA programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All PA activities must avoid biased or misleading content intended to manipulate audiences; adhere to principles of information and tenets of PA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Security review is the process of reviewing information and products prior to public release to ensure the material will not jeopardize ongoing or future operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clear authorities and procedures for security review in PAG; perform reviews early and efficiently to avoid unnecessary delays while protecting OPSEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA Resourcing and Force Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: PA activities require facilities, personnel, equipment, transportation, and communications capabilities; anticipated resource requirements should be identified early and may require augmentation from supporting commands, Services, and military departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan to augment PA personnel and to procure, lease, or assign necessary resources; include Defense Media Activity and JPASE as potential sources of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of PA into Command Processes
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs and PA staffs should be involved in planning, decisionmaking, training, equipping, and executing operations and be integrated into all levels of the command with appropriate clearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed PA in operational planning (JOPP), ensure PA representation on staff, and synchronize PA actions with operational and interagency processes to maintain unity of effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Pooling Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A media pool is a limited number of news media who represent a larger number of news organizations for news gathering and material sharing when resources cannot accommodate many journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pooling to facilitate coverage when access/resources are limited; establish clear selection, sharing, and distribution rules to maintain fairness and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of News (Newsworthiness Criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of news that make information more newsworthy include impact, timeliness, prominence, oddity, conflict, and proximity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider these elements when crafting releases and selecting imagery; anticipate what aspects of an event will attract attention and how adversaries might exploit them.
